units.left_text: A revelation about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
units.right_text: This is the burden against Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:

units.left_text: The LORD is a jealous God and avenges. The LORD avenges and is full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he maintains wrath against his enemies.
units.right_text: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God;

units.left_text: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
units.right_text: The LORD is slow to anger

units.left_text: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel languish. The flower of Lebanon languishes.
units.right_text: He rebukes the sea and dries it up;

units.left_text: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at his presence, yes, the world, and all who dwell in it.
units.right_text: The mountains quake before Him,

units.left_text: Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the fierceness of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken apart by him.
units.right_text: Who can withstand His indignation?

units.left_text: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
units.right_text: The LORD is good,

units.left_text: But with an overflowing flood, he will make a full end of her place, and will pursue his enemies into darkness.
units.right_text: But with an overwhelming flood

units.left_text: What do you plot against the LORD? He will make a full end. Affliction won’t rise up the second time.
units.right_text: Whatever you plot against the LORD,

units.left_text: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.
units.right_text: For they will be entangled as with thorns

units.left_text: One has gone out of you who devises evil against the LORD, who counsels wickedness.
units.right_text: From you, O Nineveh, comes forth

units.left_text: The LORD says: “Though they are in full strength and likewise many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
units.right_text: This is what the LORD says:

units.left_text: Now I will break his yoke from off you, and will burst your bonds apart.”
units.right_text: For I will now break their yoke from your neck

units.left_text: The LORD has commanded concerning you: “No more descendants will bear your name. Out of the house of your gods, I will cut off the engraved image and the molten image. I will make your grave, for you are vile.”
units.right_text: The LORD has issued a command concerning you, O Nineveh:

units.left_text: Behold, on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace! Keep your feasts, Judah! Perform your vows, for the wicked one will no more pass through you. He is utterly cut off.
units.right_text: Look to the mountains—

units.left_text: He who dashes in pieces has come up against you. Keep the fortress! Watch the way! Strengthen your waist! Fortify your power mightily!
units.right_text: One who scatters advances

units.left_text: For the LORD restores the excellency of Jacob as the excellency of Israel, for the destroyers have destroyed them and ruined their vine branches.
units.right_text: For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob

units.left_text: The shield of his mighty men is made red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished.
units.right_text: The shields of his mighty men are red;

units.left_text: The chariots rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the wide ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
units.right_text: The chariots dash through the streets;

units.left_text: He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.
units.right_text: He summons his nobles;

units.left_text: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
units.right_text: The river gates are thrown open

units.left_text: It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her servants moan as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.
units.right_text: It is decreed that the city be exiled

units.left_text: But Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water, yet they flee away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one looks back.
units.right_text: Nineveh has been like a pool of water

units.left_text: Take the plunder of silver. Take the plunder of gold, for there is no end of treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
units.right_text: “Plunder the silver!

units.left_text: She is empty, void, and waste. The heart melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and faces have grown pale.
units.right_text: She is emptied!

units.left_text: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked with the lion’s cubs, and no one made them afraid?
units.right_text: Where is the lions’ lair

units.left_text: The lion tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled prey for his lionesses, and filled his caves with the kill and his dens with prey.
units.right_text: The lion mauled enough for its cubs

units.left_text: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
units.right_text: “Behold, I am against you,”

units.left_text: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery—no end to the prey.
units.right_text: Woe to the city of blood,

units.left_text: The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
units.right_text: The crack of the whip,

units.left_text: the horseman charging, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies
units.right_text: Charging horseman,

units.left_text: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
units.right_text: because of the many harlotries of the harlot,

units.left_text: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
units.right_text: “Behold, I am against you,”

units.left_text: I will throw abominable filth on you and make you vile, and will make you a spectacle.
units.right_text: I will pelt you with filth

units.left_text: It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
units.right_text: Then all who see you

units.left_text: Are you better than No-Amon, who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?
units.right_text: Are you better than Thebes,

units.left_text: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
units.right_text: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength;

units.left_text: Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
units.right_text: Yet she became an exile;

units.left_text: You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
units.right_text: You too will become drunk;

units.left_text: All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs. If they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
units.right_text: All your fortresses are fig trees

units.left_text: Behold, your troops among you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
units.right_text: Look at your troops —

units.left_text: Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
units.right_text: Draw your water for the siege;

units.left_text: There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
units.right_text: There the fire will devour you;

units.left_text: You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips and flees away.
units.right_text: You have multiplied your merchants

units.left_text: Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
units.right_text: Your guards are like the swarming locust,

units.left_text: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
units.right_text: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber;

units.left_text: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
units.right_text: There is no healing for your injury;
